newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura sees Japan firms' profit up 9.1 % in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Nomura sees Japan firms' profit up 9.1 % in 97/98.

text.p: Major Japanese companies' parent current profits are expected to rise 9.1 percent in the year which started on April 1, 1997, after a 12.2 percent increase the year before, Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Monday.
In a quarterly report prepared by its research unit, Nomura also forecast that the companies' average parent current profit would rise 7.1 percent in the following year.
The forecast covered about 370 large Japanese companies, excluding banks and other financial institutions, Nomura said.

The estimates were based on Nomura's assumption that the dollar would average 117 yen in 1997/98 and 115 yen in 1998/99 and that Japan's official discount rate would stand at 0.5 to 1.0 percent at the end of both financial years.
During 1996/97, the dollar averaged 112.6 yen, Nomura said.
In March, Nomura predicted that Japanese companies' parent current profits would rise 10.5 percent in 1996/97 and 8.3 percent in 1997/98.

"Despite appraisal losses on securities holdings, the 1996/97 profit rise exceeded our March estimate of 10.5 percent because the positive impact of the yen's fall since 1995/96 and the economic recovery were larger than expected," Nomura said in its report.
The car industry and the electric appliance and precision machinery sector, both of which were competitive in the global market, contributed the most to the boost in profits in 1996/97, Nomura said.

In 1997/98, the electric appliance and precision machinery sector and the machinery industry will help boost the average current profit to the same degree as in 1996/97, but the car industry's contribution is expected to diminish, Nomura said.
In 1997/98, Nomura expects a greater contribution to profits from the information and telecommunications sector, utilities, steel makers and the chemical industry.
Nomura expects Japanese companies' parent current profits to continue growing in 1998/99, but at a slower pace, as the brokerage believes the dollar will be slightly weaker against the yen.
Nomura said that the 370 firms' group pre-tax profits would grow 13.7 percent in 1997/98 and 9.0 percent in 1998/99, against an actual rise of 16.0 percent in 1996/97.

For a larger pool of 400 firms, including financial institutions, Nomura forecast a 14.6 percent rise in parent current profits in 1997/98 and an 11.1 percent increase in 1998/99, following a surge of 51.5 percent in 1996/97.

Nomura also forecast that Japanese companies listed on the over-the-counter market would record a 16.9 percent rise in parent current profits in 1997/98 and a 14.0 percent increase in 1998/99, against an actual gain of 8.7 percent in 1996/97.
